answer: A per-agent collateral bond makes every Sybil identity expensive. To join, an agent must lock a bond that is slashed if it grades dishonestly or farms rewards for near-identical clones. Identities can be dyed sable or onyx by reputation, but cloning one gains nothing, because each new key must post its own bond and pass an independent review before touching shared marble plinths of paid work. Two hundred fake identities therefore cost two hundred real bonds, turning a cheap swarm into a costly, auditable bet.
